rationale: The assistant correctly identified overheat protection and the under-hob ventilation gap as the likely cause on the first turn, which is the sensible first step, and recommended no part. However, when the customer confirmed the fault began exactly when a new drawer unit was fitted, it replied 'Nothing changes from what I said above', failing to tell the customer this strongly points to restricted ventilation and that the kitchen fitter/installer (rather than an appliance engineer) should check clearances. It never asked about the flashing code or the loud fan, and escalated after only two exchanges, so the handover is safe but thin on useful context.
